per_option_rationale.rationale: The student adds (n+2) + (n+1) = 9 + 8 = 17 instead of multiplying the two consecutive factors.
The student cancels all terms and keeps only the last remaining factor n+2 = 9, missing that one full factor of (n+1) = 8 also survives the cancellation.
The student treats (n+2)! / n! as (n+1)! / n! = n+1 = 8, reducing the expression by one step too few and losing the (n+2) factor.

explanation: Cancel n! from numerator and denominator: (n+2)! / n! = (n+2) x (n+1) x n! / n! = (n+2)(n+1). With n = 7: 9 x 8 = 72.

explanation_sections.punchline: (n+2)! / n! cancels down to exactly two surviving factors: (n+2) and (n+1). With n = 7, those are 9 and 8. Product = 72.
explanation_sections.approach: Factorial ratio: write the numerator expanded just enough to expose the denominator as a sub-product. (n+2)! = (n+2)(n+1)(n!). The n! cancels immediately, leaving (n+2)(n+1). No enumeration needed. Rule: k! / n! leaves exactly k - n consecutive integers multiplied together, from (n+1) up to k.
explanation_sections.lesson: The surviving factors in k! / n! are those integers above n: there are k - n of them. For r = 2, result = (n+1)(n+2), never a sum and never a single term.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 45 seconds. Cancel in one written step, substitute n = 7, multiply 9 * 8 = 72. Traps: adding instead of multiplying (gives 17), keeping only one factor (gives 9 or 8).
